name: Urge Overkill
label: Touch and Go
lede: Nash Kato and Eddie "King" Roeser met at Northwestern, took to lounge suits and medallions, found a drummer called Blackie Onassis, and cut a Neil Diamond cover on a whim that Quentin Tarantino used for Uma Thurman's dance in Pulp Fiction.

eras.title: Two students, one Parliament lyric
eras.text: Kato and Roeser met at Northwestern and started a band in Chicago. Steve Albini, who had shared a place with them, recorded the first records, scrappy and loud.

years.h: A guy named Nathan Kaatrud meets Eddie "King" Roeser at Northwestern
years.p: Kaatrud, who will become Nash Kato, and Roeser are students at Northwestern University in Evanston, Illinois. Urge Overkill is a year away.

years.h: Urge Overkill takes its name from a Parliament song
years.p: Nash Kato, Roeser and drummer Pat Byrne start the band in Chicago. The phrase comes from [[Parliament|d1947987-9614-49ae-bd36-8000e6b6f7d0]]'s "Funkentelechy".

years.h: Steve Albini produces the first EP, Strange, I..., for Ruthless
years.p: Urge Overkill's debut comes out on Ruthless Records. A standalone single, "Lineman", follows in 1987.
years.xp: Albini had shared a place with the band, and he went on to record their first three records. Wikipedia's Albini entry says he co-managed Ruthless in Chicago with John Kezdy of the Effigies and Jon Babbin of Criminal IQ Records.

years.h: Jesus Urge Superstar starts the Touch and Go years
years.p: Albini produces again, with Kriss Bataille now on drums. It is the band's first full-length and their first release on Touch and Go.

eras.title: Suits, medallions and a song cut on a whim
eras.text: Butch Vig and Albini sharpened the sound, Blackie Onassis took the drum stool, and the matching suits and gold medallions became the act. By 1992 they were opening for Nirvana and had recorded the song that would change things.

years.h: Butch Vig produces Americruiser, and college radio listens
years.p: Jack "Jaguar" Watt of Baron Lesh plays drums. Wikipedia calls the sound a Stonesy fusion of arena rock and punk, and the album builds a college-radio following.

years.big: "I'm Blackie Onassis because I drum in Urge."
years.src: Wikipedia: The Supersonic Storybook · Stereogum: Urge Overkill drummer
years.h: Johnny Rowan becomes Blackie Onassis
years.p: Rowan joins for the third album, produced by Albini. Jim Ellison of [[Material Issue|35290bf2-aa8e-412d-8f4e-0b3362044958]], a friend of the band, came up with the title.
years.xp:
Kato and Roeser already had stage personas, and the new drummer got one too. The line above is how Rowan explained the name, as Stereogum quotes him.

Critics split on the record. Robert Christgau gave it a C; Spin covered it favorably. Nine tracks, 38:55, one co-written by Kato and Onassis.

years.h: Opening for Nirvana on the Nevermind tour
years.p: Urge Overkill plays support on [[Nirvana|5b11f4ce-a62d-471e-81fc-a69a8278c7da]]'s American tour, then leaves Touch and Go for Geffen. The label switch draws criticism.

years.src: Wikipedia: Stull · Wikipedia: Exile in Guyville
years.h: Stull puts a Kansas cemetery on the cover and a Neil Diamond song on the EP
years.p: [[Kramer|d898e082-70d1-4a86-ac8e-ecdf89892994]] produces. Roeser says the cover of [[Neil Diamond|a42d3fd5-55de-4206-86c3-4fbb5404018f]]'s "Girl, You'll Be a Woman Soon" was a decision made on the spot.
years.xp:
The cover photo was shot at Stull Cemetery near Lawrence, Kansas. The tombstone marks the grave of Isaac Stull, the town's namesake; urban legends since the 1970s call the cemetery one of seven portals to Hell.

A second cover, "Stitches" by the Alan Milman Sect, sits alongside the originals. Spin's Johan Kugelberg called the EP "pretty close to flawless" and the Diamond cover "mind-boggling".

The closer, "Goodbye to Guyville", gave [[Liz Phair|149326c2-b8a3-48e3-b3d2-9b5b9593127f]] the title for Exile in Guyville, and Kato took and cropped the photo on that album's cover.
play: Girl, You'll Be a Woman Soon

eras.title: Saturation point
eras.text: The move to Geffen was a bid for a hit, and it landed: "Sister Havana" on rock radio, a Pearl Jam tour, then Pulp Fiction. Their old producer Steve Albini answered in print.

years.h: Geffen gets Saturation, and "Sister Havana" reaches No. 6
years.p: Recorded with the Butcher Bros. from December 17, 1992 to January 9, 1993. Kato sings lead on most of it, not Roeser.
years.xp:
"Sister Havana" hit No. 6 on Billboard's Modern Rock chart and No. 10 on Mainstream Rock. Four singles came off the record: that one, "Dropout", "Bottle of Fur" and "Positive Bleeding".

The album peaked at No. 146 on the Billboard 200 and No. 16 in Australia. Nielsen SoundScan counted 277,000 U.S. copies as of 2013. Entertainment Weekly gave it a B+; the Spin Alternative Record Guide gave it 8 out of 10. The cover art is the Houston skyline.

yt: Live at Cabaret Metro, Chicago, June 10, 1993
years.h: Pearl Jam's openers also donate "Take a Walk" to No Alternative
years.p: Urge Overkill supports [[Pearl Jam|83b9cbe7-9857-49e2-ab8e-b57b01038103]] on the Vs. tour and gives the song to the Red Hot Organization's AIDS benefit album.

years.h: Steve Albini turns the Chicago Reader on his old clients
years.p: His January 27 letter, "Three Pandering Sluts", puts Urge Overkill in a row with [[Liz Phair|149326c2-b8a3-48e3-b3d2-9b5b9593127f]] and [[The Smashing Pumpkins|ba0d6274-db14-4ef5-b28d-657ebde1a396]].
years.xp: Albini had produced three Urge Overkill records and once shared a place with the band. In the same letter he called Phair "a fucking chore to listen to" and the Pumpkins "ultimately insignificant".

years.h: Quentin Tarantino picks a two-year-old cover for Uma Thurman to dance to
years.p: "Girl, You'll Be a Woman Soon" reaches No. 59 on the Billboard Hot 100 and No. 37 in the UK after Pulp Fiction.
years.xp:
Roeser's account of how it happened: "Apparently, Quentin was familiar with us, and he picks all the songs for his movies." He has said Tarantino settled on it after talking it over with Thurman, who dances to it in the film.

The band had cut it on a whim for Stull in 1992.

eras.title: Exit the Dragon, exit King
eras.text: The follow-up did best in Australia. Onassis referred to his heroin use on the record, Kato and Roeser stopped getting along, and by 1997 Urge Overkill was two men on a Sony imprint, and then nobody.

years.h: Australia puts Exit the Dragon at No. 6, the U.S. at 129
years.p: The second Geffen album. On "The Mistake", Blackie Onassis refers to his own drug use.

years.h: Blackie Onassis is arrested for heroin possession
years.p: Not long after Exit the Dragon, the drummer is arrested, Stereogum reported. He struggled with addiction through the mid-1990s.

years.h: Roeser walks out after clashing with Nash Kato
years.p: He goes on to play with ex-[[The Jesus Lizard|dfebd6c0-dae7-4cc8-a8e9-0dbaa382209f]] drummer [[Jim Kimball|93ed63b4-5dc3-4f4d-9a74-b891e0354b76]] as L.I.M.E., and with his brother John in Electric Airlines.

years.h: Two men sign to Sony's 550 Music, and no album follows
years.p: Kato and Onassis are what's left of Urge Overkill. The first run of the band ends here.

eras.title: Debutante, and the suits come back out
eras.text: Kato made a solo record. In 2004 he and Roeser patched things up and took the suits back on stage without Onassis. A new album took until 2011.

years.h: Nash Kato goes solo with Debutante
years.p: Onassis co-writes six of its 13 songs and plays on it. It is the last music he makes with Kato before losing touch with the band.

years.cap: Nash Kato and Eddie Roeser trading guitar licks, May 2005
years.h: Kato and Roeser reunite without Blackie Onassis
years.p: Mike "Hadji" Hodgkiss plays bass, Chris Frantisak keys and Nate Arling drums. They play the Troubadour, Double Door, First Avenue and the Bowery Ballroom, then Europe and Australia.

years.cap: Nash Kato at the Starlight, May 2005
years.h: Maxwell's in Hoboken becomes the comeback live album
years.p: The reunion show is released as Live at Maxwell's 2/5/04 on eMusicLive.

years.cap: Urge Overkill at Bumbershoot, Seattle, September 2011
yt: "Girl, You'll Be a Woman Soon" at the Tarantino roast
years.h: "Effigy" is the first new song in 15 years
years.p: New York's WRXP-FM premieres it. On December 1, 2010, the band plays the roast of Quentin Tarantino.

years.h: A self-released Rock & Roll Submarine ends a 16-year wait
years.p: On October 8, 2011, the band opens for [[Weezer|6fe07aa5-fec0-4eca-a456-f29bff451b04]] at Riot Fest at Chicago's Congress Theater.

eras.title: Oui, and goodbye to Blackie
eras.text: A second comeback album came in 2022. A year later the drummer from the Geffen years died at 57.

years.h: Oui lands on Omnivore Recordings
years.p: Kato and Roeser make the first album in 11 years with brothers Nate and Adam Arling on drums and bass.

years.src: Stereogum: Urge Overkill drummer · Wikipedia: Urge Overkill
years.h: Johnny Rowan, the original Blackie Onassis, dies at 57
years.p: Urge Overkill's statement did not give a cause of death. Rowan drummed on Saturation, Exit the Dragon and the Pulp Fiction cover.
years.xp:
The band's full statement, per Stereogum: "Urge Overkill is saddened to report that Blackie has passed away." It was posted June 14, 2023; Wikipedia dates the death June 13.

Rowan sat out the 2004 reunion and everything after it.

years.h: Exit the Dragon turns 30 on pink and purple vinyl
years.p: Porterhouse Records reissues it as a limited pressing.
